flag.uninstall_purge: also delete the data directory (devices, keys, accounts, logs, backups)
flag.uninstall_dry_run: only print what would be removed

install.need_root: run as root: sudo kut install
install.no_bash: bash is required to run the installer: {err}

uninstall.need_root: run as root: sudo kut uninstall
uninstall.plan_head: Kut will be removed from this server:
uninstall.step_firewall: remove the KUT-* chains and Kut's jumps in INPUT, FORWARD and nat POSTROUTING (IPv4 and IPv6)
uninstall.step_ufw: remove the ufw rule {port}/udp that the Kut installer added
uninstall.step_no_ufw: leave ufw and Docker rules alone (the installer did not add a ufw rule)
uninstall.step_keep: keep the data directory {data} (use -purge to delete it)
uninstall.forward_note: net.ipv4.ip_forward stays on until the next reboot (other services such as Docker may rely on it).
uninstall.need_yes: standard input is not a terminal: pass -yes to confirm
uninstall.backup_written: Backup written: {path} (encrypted; restore with: kut restore -f {path})
uninstall.bad_data: refusing to delete {data}: -purge needs a Kut data directory (with server.json) at an absolute path other than /
uninstall.iface_up: the interface {iface} is still up, so Kut's firewall rules were left in place (removing them could let traffic through). Run: sudo wg-quick down {iface} && sudo kut uninstall
